title: Naval Topic 6 生词 · 英英解释

items.ex: Not only means not just this one thing. There is something more, and often it is even bigger. We say not only this, but also that.
exs: She's not only my lash artist, she's also my friend.
This glue not only dries fast, it also lasts longer.

src.t: And the journey is not only the reward, the journey is the only thing there is.

items.ex: A reward is something good you get because you did something well or worked hard. It is like a prize at the end.
exs: A happy client is the best reward.
After a long week, I give myself a small reward.

src.t: And the journey is not only the reward, the journey is the only thing there is.

items.ex: Human nature is the way all people naturally think and act. It is not learned. Everybody is born with it.
exs: It's human nature to want to be liked.
Getting bored is just human nature.

src.t: Even success, it’s human nature to bank it very quickly, right,

items.zh: 把它存起来；当成理所当然
items.ex: To bank something is to put it away, like money in a bank, and then stop thinking about it. Naval means you get success and quickly treat it as normal.
exs: She got the promotion, banked it, and started chasing the next goal.
Don't just bank your wins. Enjoy them for a moment.

src.t: Even success, it’s human nature to bank it very quickly, right,

items.ex: A loop is a circle that goes round and round and comes back to the start. When you loop, you repeat the same thing again and again.
exs: I'm stuck in a loop of working, sleeping and working again.
The song keeps looping in my head.

src.t: because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you’re bored, then you want something,

items.ex: To run through something means to go through it from the start to the end. A loop we run through is a pattern we go through again and again.
exs: Let's run through the steps before the client comes.
We all run through the same worries.

src.t: because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you’re bored, then you want something,

items.ex: To sit around means to sit and do nothing useful, usually because you are bored or lazy.
exs: I don't want to sit around all weekend.
We just sat around waiting for the client.

src.t: because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you’re bored, then you want something,

items.ex: To decide means to make a choice in your mind. After you decide, you know what you will do or believe.
exs: I decided to take a lash course.
You decide how you feel about it.

src.t: then when you want something you decide you’re not gonna be happy until you get that thing,

items.ex: A bout is a short time when something happens strongly, often something bad, like a bout of illness or a bout of sadness.
exs: I had a bout of the flu last week.
Everyone has a bout of self-doubt sometimes.

src.t: then you start your bout of suffering or anticipation while you strive to get that thing.

items.ex: Anticipation is the feeling of waiting for something that will happen. It can be excited or nervous.
exs: The anticipation before a big event is exciting.
She waited in anticipation for the results.

src.t: then you start your bout of suffering or anticipation while you strive to get that thing.

items.ex: To strive means to try very hard to get something. It is a little more serious than try.
exs: I strive to make every set perfect.

src.t: then you start your bout of suffering or anticipation while you strive to get that thing.

items.ex: To get used to something means it slowly starts to feel normal. At first it is new, then it is not special anymore.
exs: I got used to waking up early.
You'll get used to the new tweezers.

src.t: If you get that thing then you get used to it, and then you get bored again,

items.ex: For a bit means for a short time. It is a casual way to say for a little while.
exs: Can you wait for a bit?
I was sad for a bit, then I felt fine.

src.t: then a few months later you want something else, and if you don’t get it then you’re unhappy for a bit, and then you get over it then you want something else.

items.ex: To get over something means to feel okay again after something bad, like a sickness, a problem or a sad time.
exs: It took me a month to get over the breakup.
You'll get over it. Give it time.

src.t: then a few months later you want something else, and if you don’t get it then you’re unhappy for a bit, and then you get over it then you want something else.

items.ex: A cycle is a set of things that happen again and again in the same order. When it ends, it starts again.
exs: Lashes grow in a natural cycle.
Let's break the cycle of stress.

src.t: That’s the normal cycle. So whether you’re happy or unhappy at the end, it tends not to last.

items.ex: We use whether … or to say it does not matter which one. The result is the same in both cases.
exs: Whether you're tired or not, be kind to clients.
Whether it rains or shines, I go to work.

src.t: That’s the normal cycle. So whether you’re happy or unhappy at the end, it tends not to last.

items.ex: If something tends to happen, it usually happens. It is not always, but most of the time.
exs: Clients tend to book more before holidays.
I tend to talk fast when I'm nervous.

src.t: That’s the normal cycle. So whether you’re happy or unhappy at the end, it tends not to last.

items.ex: To last means to continue for a time. If a feeling does not last, it goes away soon.
exs: These lashes last about four weeks.

src.t: That’s the normal cycle. So whether you’re happy or unhappy at the end, it tends not to last.

items.ex: Glib means saying something too easily, without thinking deeply. A glib answer sounds smooth but is not careful or serious.
exs: Don't give me a glib answer. Tell me what you really think.
It's easy to be glib about other people's problems.

src.t: Now I don’t wanna be glib and say that there’s no point in making money or being successful.

items.ex: If there is no point in doing something, it is useless. It will not help or change anything.
exs: There's no point in worrying about it now.
There's no point in arguing with him.

src.t: Now I don’t wanna be glib and say that there’s no point in making money or being successful.

items.ex: Absolutely means completely, or yes, for sure. People also say Absolutely! to agree strongly.
exs: Can I book for Friday? Absolutely!

src.t: There absolutely is—money solves all your money problems, so it is good to have money.

items.ex: To solve means to find an answer to a problem, so the problem is gone.
exs: Money can solve some problems, but not all.

src.t: There absolutely is—money solves all your money problems, so it is good to have money.

items.ex: That said means even so. You say it after one idea, before you add a different or opposite idea.
exs: The course is expensive. That said, it's really good.
I love my job. That said, I'm tired.

src.t: That said, there are those stories, I don’t know if you’ve seen those studies, I don’t know how real these are, a lot of these psych studies don’t replicate,

items.ex: Psych is a short, casual word for psychology, the study of the mind. Psych studies are experiments about how people think and feel.
exs: Psych studies show that sleep helps memory.
I read a psych study about happiness.

src.t: That said, there are those stories, I don’t know if you’ve seen those studies, I don’t know how real these are, a lot of these psych studies don’t replicate,

items.ex: When a study replicates, other scientists do it again and get the same result. If it doesn't replicate, the result may not be true.
exs: Can you replicate this lash style?

src.t: That said, there are those stories, I don’t know if you’ve seen those studies, I don’t know how real these are, a lot of these psych studies don’t replicate,

items.ex: To break your back means to badly hurt your back bone in an accident. People also say it to mean work extremely hard.
exs: He broke his back in a car accident.
I broke my back to finish all the sets today.

src.t: but it’s a fun little study that shows that people who break their back and people who win the lottery are back to their baseline happiness two years later.

items.ex: A lottery is a game where you buy a ticket and a few lucky people win a lot of money by chance.
exs: If I won the lottery, I'd open a big salon.
Winning the lottery doesn't make you happy forever.

src.t: but it’s a fun little study that shows that people who break their back and people who win the lottery are back to their baseline happiness two years later.

items.ex: A baseline is your normal level, the starting point before anything changes. Baseline happiness is how happy you usually are.
exs: After the trip, my mood went back to baseline.

src.t: but it’s a fun little study that shows that people who break their back and people who win the lottery are back to their baseline happiness two years later.

items.ex: Yep is a very casual way to say yes. People say it in friendly talk.

src.t: Yep.

items.ex: Entirely means completely, one hundred percent. Not entirely true means partly true.

src.t: Again, don’t know if that’s entirely true. I think money can buy you happiness if you earned it,

items.ex: To earn means to get money or something good because you worked for it. Earned money feels different from free money.
exs: I earned this money with my own hands.

src.t: Again, don’t know if that’s entirely true. I think money can buy you happiness if you earned it,

items.ex: Along the way means during the journey, while you are going toward your goal.
exs: I made many friends along the way.
You'll learn a lot along the way.

src.t: because then along the way you have both pride and confidence in yourself, and you have a sense of accomplishment,

items.ex: Pride is the good feeling you have when you or someone close to you does something well.
exs: She looked at her work with pride.

src.t: because then along the way you have both pride and confidence in yourself, and you have a sense of accomplishment,

items.ex: Confidence is the feeling that you can do something well. You trust yourself.
exs: Speaking English every day builds confidence.

src.t: because then along the way you have both pride and confidence in yourself, and you have a sense of accomplishment,

items.ex: An accomplishment is something good you finished after hard work. A sense of accomplishment is the proud feeling after that.
exs: Opening my studio was a big accomplishment.
Finishing a hard set gives me a sense of accomplishment.

src.t: because then along the way you have both pride and confidence in yourself, and you have a sense of accomplishment,

items.ex: To set out to do something means to start with a clear plan or goal to do it.
exs: I set out to learn English in six months.
She set out to build her own brand.

src.t: and you set out to do something and you were right, so I’ll bet that lingers, and then as I said, it solves your money problems.

items.ex: I'll bet means I am pretty sure. It is like saying I would bet money that it is true.
exs: I'll bet she's tired after work.
I'll bet you'll love these lashes.

src.t: and you set out to do something and you were right, so I’ll bet that lingers, and then as I said, it solves your money problems.

items.ex: To linger means to stay longer than expected and go away slowly. A feeling or a smell can linger.
exs: The smell of coffee lingered in the room.
Her kind words lingered in my mind.

src.t: and you set out to do something and you were right, so I’ll bet that lingers, and then as I said, it solves your money problems.

items.ex: In general means usually, or when you look at the whole picture, not small details.
exs: In general, clients like natural styles.
In general, I'm a happy person.

src.t: So I don’t want to be too glib about it, but I would say in general, this loop that we run through of desire, dopamine, fulfillment, unfulfillment—you have to enjoy the journey.

items.ex: Dopamine is a chemical in your brain. It gives you a feeling of wanting and reward, like when you get a like on social media.
exs: Checking your phone gives you a little hit of dopamine.

src.t: So I don’t want to be too glib about it, but I would say in general, this loop that we run through of desire, dopamine, fulfillment, unfulfillment—you have to enjoy the journey.

items.ex: Fulfillment is the deep happy feeling when you get what you wanted or do something meaningful. Unfulfillment is the opposite.
exs: I find fulfillment in helping clients feel beautiful.

src.t: So I don’t want to be too glib about it, but I would say in general, this loop that we run through of desire, dopamine, fulfillment, unfulfillment—you have to enjoy the journey.

items.ex: Ninety-nine percent means 99 out of 100. People use it to mean almost all.
exs: Ninety-nine percent of my clients come back.

src.t: The journey is all there is. Ninety-nine percent of your time is spent on the journey, so what kind of a journey is it if you’re not going to enjoy it?

items.ex: To spend time or money on something means to use it for that thing.
exs: I spend two hours on each full set.
Don't spend all your money on clothes.

src.t: The journey is all there is. Ninety-nine percent of your time is spent on the journey, so what kind of a journey is it if you’re not going to enjoy it?
